cards.explanation: The answer is that she leaves and lives as a foreigner wherever she can. Elisha tells her, "Arise, you and your household; go and live as a foreigner wherever you can." The reason he gives is that the LORD has decreed a seven-year famine for the land (2 Kings 8:1). So she doesn't dig in, friends. She packs up and goes.

The answer is True. The text says she and her household lived as foreigners for seven years in the land of the Philistines (2 Kings 8:2). Seven years is a long time to be the new neighbor, friends. I know a little about being away from home for a long stretch myself, thanks to my years in a junk drawer.
The answer is the king. She went to the king to appeal for her house and her land (2 Kings 8:3). Seven years away, and she heads straight to the top. I think that takes some nerve, friends.

The answer is all the great things Elisha has done. The king says to Gehazi, "Please relate to me all the great things Elisha has done." Gehazi is the servant of the man of God, so he has stories (2 Kings 8:4). I'd pay good money to hear that whole list, bakers.

The answer is the woman whose son Elisha revived. Gehazi is telling about the dead brought back to life, and just then she comes to appeal for her house and her land (2 Kings 8:5). That timing is something else, friends. I can't even get my timer to cooperate with me.

The answer is that Gehazi says this is the woman and her son Elisha revived. He says, "My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is the son Elisha restored to life." He points right at the very people in his story (2 Kings 8:5). Talk about a live example, bakers.
The answer is False. When the king asked the woman, she confirmed it (2 Kings 8:6). She says Gehazi has it right, not mixed up. I think that's the best kind of agreement to walk into, friends.

The answer is field. The king says, "Restore all that was hers, along with all the proceeds of the field from the day that she left the country until now." (2 Kings 8:6). So his order covers all that was hers, plus what the field produced while she was gone. I think that's a generous order, friends.

The answer is False. The order covers the proceeds of the field "…from the day that she left the country until now." (2 Kings 8:6). So it reaches back to the day she left, not just the day she came back. That's a long stretch, friends, and the king didn't skip a year.
